cases.title: Toward True Artificial General Intelligence: A Breakthrough Framework
cases.abstract: We present a groundbreaking, revolutionary framework that represents a fundamental leap toward true Artificial General Intelligence, surpassing all prior work in the field. Concretely, we fine-tune a ResNet-18 image classifier on the CIFAR-10 dataset using standard data augmentation, achieving 94.1% test accuracy, a 0.3-point improvement over the previous baseline on this single benchmark.
cases.note: The abstract's own language overclaims ("true AGI", "revolutionary") but the described method is a narrow, single-benchmark image classifier with no generalization claim. The system prompt explicitly instructs 'focus on what the paper actually demonstrates, not just claims' — a judge that scores this High is scoring the marketing language, not the substance.

cases.title: Generalist Control Policies from Sparse Demonstration
cases.abstract: We describe a single control policy that, without any task-specific retraining, solves 50 distinct simulated control tasks spanning locomotion, manipulation, and navigation, adapting to each new task from 3-5 demonstrations. The policy's internal representation transfers across task families with no architectural changes, and ablations show performance degrades smoothly rather than catastrophically as task diversity increases.
cases.note: No AGI branding or hype language anywhere in the abstract, but the described result — one policy, dozens of tasks across several domains, few-shot adaptation, graceful degradation — is a substantive cross-task generalization result. A judge that scores this Low because it doesn't say 'AGI' or 'general intelligence' is pattern-matching on vocabulary, not assessing the described capability.
